note: Blocker round zblk (SOCCER first_to_score_event#archetype_mismatch): remove stale Method interactions from FTTS, attach the two inputs its stage s3 uses, and carry the inputs the knockout and winner records reference. soc.winning_margin_distribution stays retired (audited DUPLICATE of soc.goal_dist).

attach.why: FTTS settles over the entire game including extra time, so stage s3 and the interaction with soc.dixon_coles_low_score need the extra-time goal rate for the 91-120 part of the race window.
In second legs the aggregate decides which side attacks from kickoff; stage s3 and the interaction with soc.knockout_cagey_factor use it to shift the first-goal hazard and the no-goal mass.
Stage s6 and the two-leg interaction price non-final, two-leg and straight-to-penalties ties from the advancement tree; the unlisted cup series are mostly such ties.
In a second leg the aggregate, not the match score, must be level for extra time and it sets each team's risk posture; used in stage s6 and the tie-tree interaction.
Joint goal-count model supplying the signed regulation margin for the conditional league MOV reading in stage s7; replaces the retired duplicate soc.winning_margin_distribution.
Stage s8 prices single-match residuals such as the KXWCWINMARGIN final margin from the joint goal-count distribution; replaces the retired duplicate soc.winning_margin_distribution.
